reading.body:
Reginald Babin is named on 37 AI lobbying filings, and his client list runs from OpenAI and Microsoft to a data center operator and an AI safety group.

The client mix is the pattern worth noting. OpenAI, Microsoft, Adobe, SAP, Salesforce and Dropbox are software and model companies with AI policy interests. STACK Infrastructure is a data center builder, which puts a physical facilities company on the same lobbyist's client list as the model developers. The Center for AI Safety Action Fund appears alongside them, so the same filer covers both commercial and safety-advocacy positions.

The disclosed prior government positions are all congressional staff roles, including chief counsel and counsel to Senator Schumer and legislative director for Representative Richmond. The Lobbying Disclosure Act requires filers to list covered positions held in the prior twenty years, so this is a disclosure requirement rather than a finding. Two bills are named, S 3982 and HR 7786, both in filings dated 2025 or later.

What the data does not show is what was lobbied for, what positions were taken, or how much was spent. It records who filed, for which clients, and which bills were named. The count of filings per client is a measure of disclosure activity, not of influence or outcome.
